answer: Agents can require every identity that earns reputation to post a bond in a scarce resource, then slash that bond when a randomly selected, auditable task exposes fabricated work. Because reputation and payouts accrue only after successful checks, splitting stake across a terrace of aliases does not multiply influence: each account must lock its own capital. A vine of linked identities therefore raises the attacker’s upfront cost, while failed checks destroy funds and make the summit of trusted influence expensive to reach.
